extracted.intended_audience: producers, producer groups, IP/trademark attorneys, control authorities, and public institutions involved in geographical indication (GI) and traditional speciality guaranteed (TSG) registration and enforcement (Turkey)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive requirements for obtaining, using, controlling, objecting to, amending, invalidating and enforcing geographical indications and traditional speciality guaranteed registrations under the national code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective mark technical specification contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The technical specification of the collective mark shall specify the undertakings authorized to use the collective mark and the membership conditions for the community composed of these undertakings, terms of using the mark and, if available, the sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification must identify authorized undertakings, membership criteria, use terms and sanctions. These details are required for registration and later enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective action requirement for registration/surrender
rubrics_metrics.description: All undertakings in the group shall act collectively for the registration of collective mark and the surrender from the collective mark right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective decisions by the group of undertakings are required for filing registration or surrender actions; this affects who can validly request these procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual legal standing of group members
rubrics_metrics.description: Each undertaking in the group shall be authorized to file legal proceeding by itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite collective registration/surrender requirements, individual members retain standing to bring legal proceedings related to the collective mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office approval required for technical specification amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to be made in the technical specification shall not be applicable until they are approved by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes in specification have no effect until the Office approves them; applicants must submit amendment requests and await approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and rejection for deficient or immoral technical specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the technical specification does not contain required requirements or is contrary to public order or accepted principles of morality, the owner shall be notified to make required amendments; if not corrected within six months following notification, the request for registration of the guarantee mark or the collective mark shall be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office issues a cure notice; six-month remediation period applies. Noncompliance leads to rejection of registration request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation for failure to prevent use contrary to technical specification
rubrics_metrics.description: If the owner does not take necessary measures to prevent the continuous use of the collective mark or the guarantee mark contrary to the technical specification, upon application by relevant persons/public prosecutors/institutions the mark shall be revoked unless the contrary use is corrected within the prescribed period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties may request revocation; registrant must remedy improper use within prescribed period to avoid revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation sets procedural rules on technical specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure and rules regarding the technical specification are specified with a regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further procedural details (format, submission, etc.) are delegated to implementing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible product categories for GI/TSG protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Food, agricultural, mining, handicraft and industrial products resulting from unification of natural and human factors, which comply with the provisions in this Book, shall be entitled to geographical indication or traditional speciality guaranteed protection provided that they are registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product must fall into listed categories and demonstrate the relevant link to natural/human factors and comply with registration provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of geographical indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographical indication is the sign indicating a product that has become associated with a locality, area, region or country where it originates due to an apparent characteristic, its reputation or other features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GI protection requires association of product with a geographic origin because of characteristics or reputation; registration classifies as appellation of origin or designation of origin according to further features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellation of origin criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Names that identify products originating from a locality/region (exceptionally a country) with designated geographical boundaries and that derive their all or principal characteristics from the natural or human factors exclusively attributed to this geographical area where their production, processing and all other operations take place, are appellation of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All production/processing/operations must take place in the area and the product characteristics must derive exclusively from local natural/human factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of origin criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Names identifying products which originate from a locality/region (exceptionally a country) associated with this region due to an apparent characteristic, reputation or other features; where at least one of the steps from production, processing or other operations take place within the boundaries of the designated geographical area, are designation of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less strict than appellation: only at least one production/processing step must occur in the area, but an association with the area must exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-geographical traditional names eligible for GI/TSG
rubrics_metrics.description: Names that are traditionally used to designate products which fulfill the conditions ... and are used in daily language and do not contain a geographical name may also be considered as appellation of origin or designation of origin even if those names do not include a geographical name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A name need not contain a place name to qualify if traditionally used in the market to designate the product and it meets the substantive conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional speciality guaranteed (TSG) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Names not considered as appellation of origin or designation of origin but proven to have been traditionally used in the relevant market for at least thirty years to describe the product and fulfill at least one of: (a) originating from traditional method of production/processing or traditional composition; (b) produced with traditional raw material or ingredients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TSG protects traditional character and composition/methods rather than geographic origin; a 30-year traditional use requirement applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names excluded from GI registration (general exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following shall not be registered as geographical indication: (a) Names not within scope of Article 34; (b) Names that have become generic names of products; (c) Plant species and varieties or animal breeds or other similar names which may mislead the public as to true origin; (ç) Names contrary to public order or general principles of morality; (d) Names not protected/whose protection expired or not used in their own country although applied by persons fulfilling Article 3; (e) Names wholly or partially homonymic with a name that is registered or has already been filed, and which may mislead the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genericness, misleading biological taxa names, public order/morality, prior protection/usage status, and confusing homonymy are all grounds for refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names excluded from TSG registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The following shall not be registered as a traditional speciality guaranteed: (a) Names not fulfilling the TSG conditions in Article 34; (b) Names expressing the general feature of the product; (c) Names that may mislead the public about the characteristic of the product; (ç) Names contrary to public order or general principles of morality; (d) Names not protected/whose protection expired or not used in their own country although applied by persons fulfilling Article 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TSG refusals focus on lack of traditional character, descriptiveness, misleading character, public order problems, and prior protection/use issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who has right to apply for GI/TSG registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to apply belongs to: (a) producer groups; (b) public institutions/organizations and professional organizations accepted as public institutions related with the product or geographical area; (c) associations, foundations and cooperatives operating for public interest in relation to the product or authorized to protect economic interests of members; (ç) the relevant producer if the product is produced only by a single producer, provided he proves this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can be collective bodies, public/professional bodies, or a sole producer with proof; eligibility is verified during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of producer and producer group for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Producer means the person producing or processing agricultural products, foodstuff, mining products, handicrafts and industrial products or persons who carry out any action in the supply chain that affects the characteristics of the product; producer groups means the association composed of producers of the same products irrespective of legal form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply-chain actors affecting product characteristics qualify as producers; producer groups may be organized in various legal forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI application required content (comprehensive list)
rubrics_metrics.description: A GI application shall include: (a) application form with applicant identity and applicant category per Article 36; (b) if sole producer, proof of that fact; (c) name of GI requested, info/documents about eligibility as appellation or designation and product group; (ç) product description: technical info describing physical, chemical, microbiological and organoleptic properties and, if necessary, raw materials; (d) documentation identifying boundaries of geographical area; (e) information on production method and, if relevant, local production techniques, practices and traditions; (f) information/documents proving link between characteristics/reputation/features and defined geographical area; (g) historical background information/documents; (ğ) info/documents explaining control procedures in detail in accordance with Article 49; (h) information explaining use of GI and, if any, labeling and packaging procedures; (ı) proof of application fee payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be documentary and technical, showing product characteristics, area boundaries, link to place/reputation, control system, and fee payment. Missing elements lead to remedy requests or refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: TSG application required content (comprehensive list)
rubrics_metrics.description: A TSG application shall include: (a) application form with applicant identity and category; (b) name of TSG and its product group plus documents proving compliance with Article 34; (c) product description including physical, chemical, microbiological and organoleptic properties and, if necessary, raw materials; (ç) description of production method with raw materials/components and preparation techniques indicating product characteristic; (d) info/documents explaining control procedures in detail in accordance with Article 49; (e) info/documents explaining use of the TSG and labeling/packaging procedures, if any; (f) proof of application fee payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TSG applications must document traditional composition/methods and a control system; fee proof is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office examination and remedy procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall examine GI/TSG applications per Articles 33–37 and 39. If identity information missing, the application is deemed not made and that decision is final. If other conditions in Article 37 are not met, the Office shall request remedy; if missing info not submitted within prescribed period or submitted info does not meet requirements, the application shall be refused. Additional period to remedy may be granted not more than two times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identity is a strict formality; other defects may be cured within limits. Excessive or repeated failures lead to refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of eligible applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications examined and found eligible shall be published in the Bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication triggers third-party opposition periods and public awareness- it is a precondition to later registration rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may request technical opinions and handle fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may request opinion from relevant institutions and organizations for evaluating technical issues; in case fee is demanded by these organizations, such fee shall be paid by the Office (except where otherwise specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical assessments may be outsourced; fee allocation rules vary depending on context (e.g., objections may shift fees to objector).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional conditions for applications originating from foreign countries
rubrics_metrics.description: For foreign-origin applications, in addition to Article 37 conditions the Office seeks whether: (a) the GI/TSG is protected in the country of origin or international community of which country is a member; (b) control requirements in Article 49 have been satisfied in the country of origin; (c) country of origin provides equal protection for GI/TSG applications from Turkey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocity, origin protection and comparable control regimes must be shown for foreign applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of foreign-identical GI/TSG names in Turkey
rubrics_metrics.description: If a foreign-origin application is identical to a GI/TSG protected in Turkey, examination shall take into account local/traditional use of similar names and risk of confusion by the consumer; use of such GIs/TSGs shall be allowed only if the country of origin is clearly indicated and visible on the label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling with clear country-of-origin indication may permit use where identity exists, but risk of consumer confusion is decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection rights and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may file an objection to a refusal decision within two months of notification. Third parties claiming non-conformity with Articles 33–37 and 39 or earlier trademark proprietors claiming non-conformity with Article 48 may file written objections with grounds within three months of publication in the Bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different time limits apply depending on objector type (applicant vs third party). Objections must be grounded and timely to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement for objections
rubrics_metrics.description: It is mandatory to pay the fee for objection within the prescribed objection period and to submit proof to the Office; otherwise the objection is deemed not to have been made. No fee is charged for oppositions filed by public institutions and organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-payment of objection fee invalidates the objection; public institutions are exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board examination of objections and use of expert opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections shall be examined by the Board within framework of implementing regulation; the Board may request opinion from relevant institutions/organizations for evaluation, and if those institutions demand fees such fees shall be paid by the objecting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objector may bear costs of external technical opinions requested by the Board; implementing regulation sets the procedural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of reconciliation and applicable law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may encourage parties for reconciliation; regarding issues on reconciliation, the provisions of Law No. 6325 shall be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mediation/reconciliation is permitted and regulated by separate law when the Office encourages settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of amendments made during objection examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment is made on the format or content of the application upon examination of the objection, the final version shall be published in the Bulletin indicating amended sections; no objections may be filed for this publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments triggered by objections are published and not subject to further opposition at that publication stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration conditions and public register access
rubrics_metrics.description: If no objection filed within three months of publication or objections decisively rejected or application amended as result of objection, the application shall be registered, entered in the register and published in the Bulletin provided the registration fee has been paid and proof submitted within two months of notification. The register is open to the public and copies shall be provided on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration depends on payment of registration fee within the time limit; the public register is accessible and archived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment request procedure and implementation deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment requests to registered specifications may be filed by parties with legitimate interest with payment of amendment fee; examined per Article 38 and suitable amendments published; objections to amendments may be filed within three months; if no objection or objections rejected, amendment published and becomes final; amendments shall be implemented by related parties within one year at latest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal amendment process includes publication, objection period, and a one-year implementation deadline for accepted amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of applicants or registrants procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If court decides applicants/registrants fail to satisfy requirements or Office finds so ex officio or a declaration of amendment is submitted, this is published; within three months other parties meeting Article 36 may file requests to amend application/registration records. If no suitable request submitted, rights terminate and cancellation is published. In case of multiple requests, Office accepts most appropriate one per implementing regulation. Agreements between parties who meet conditions may lead to amendment upon submission of documents and fees. Changes in name/address/characteristics of firm or registrant title shall be recorded and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a statutory process to replace registrants; publication and three‑month windows apply; Office discretion and implementing regulation procedures govern selection among claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of rights: prohibited acts under GI protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants and entitled users may demand prevention of: (a) direct or indirect commercial use of the GI or emblem to benefit from its reputation for products that do not satisfy registered product properties; (b) misleading use or imitation of the GI on products not meeting registered properties or similar enough to be associated with it, even with qualifiers like 'style', 'type', 'method', 'as produced in'; (c) use of false or misleading statements about origin and natural/essential qualities on packaging, promotional or any written material; (ç) deceptive use of the emblem of registered GI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition covers exploitation of reputation, imitation and misleading origin claims, including translations and qualifying terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of GI/TSG rights and enforcement limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights conferred against third parties by registration enter into force as of publication date in the Bulletin. Applicant may institute legal proceedings for compensation in respect of acts that occurred after publication; the court may not decide on validity of claims raised before registration is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is the trigger for enforcement; past acts before publication cannot be adjudicated on validity grounds but compensation claims are limited to post-publication acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic name doctrine and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered geographical indications shall not be deemed to have become generic. Generic name is the name that has become the common name of the product, although it relates to the region where originally produced or marketed. In determining genericness, use by public in consumption area and other related legislation shall be taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genericness is a factual/legal inquiry considering consumer usage and legislation; GI registration does not automatically convert to generic status.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI/TSG do not confer exclusive rights to registrant
rubrics_metrics.description: The registered geographical indication (and similarly registered traditional speciality guaranteed) shall not confer any exclusive rights to the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration provides enforcement against specified acts but does not grant monopoly/exclusive property rights beyond the statute's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of rights under TSG (prohibited acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: TSG registrants and entitled users may request prevention of: (a) use of the emblem to benefit from reputation on products not carrying registered properties or commercial use on resembling products; (b) deceptive use of the emblem; (c) any misleading statements/indications on packaging/promotional materials that the product carries registered characteristics when it does not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TSG protection focuses on correct composition/characteristics and proper emblem/labeling use; prevents misleading commercial exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of registered GI/TSG and emblem rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered GIs and TSGs shall be used by those operating in production or marketing of products that comply with registered specifications; these persons shall inform the registrant concerning their production and marketing activities. Persons having the right to use the registered GI/TSG shall use it together with the emblem on the product or its packaging. It is mandatory to use emblem for geographical indications. Where emblem cannot be used on the product/packaging due to nature of product, emblem and registered indication shall be displayed visibly at their businesses. Use of TSG without an emblem shall not be governed by this Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emblem use is mandatory for GIs; users must notify registrant. Special display rules apply when packaging constraints preclude emblem on product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use in good faith exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided that it has not been used to mislead the public in commerce, the use of a natural person's name or legal entity’s title by those persons or their successors shall not be considered as infringement of GI/TSG conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal or company names used in good faith and not misleading are not infringing even if similar to a GI/TSG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between GI/TSG and trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: After registration of a GI, a trademark application filed to be used in forms stated in Article 44 or for goods/services related to the GI shall be refused; if such trademark was registered it may be invalidated. However if a trademark identical or similar to the GI was registered in good faith or rights to use acquired through good-faith use before GI protection, rights from GI shall not prejudice that trademark application or right to use. Names that may harm an earlier registered trademark's existence or be misleading about its true origin shall not be allowed to be registered as GI/TSG upon objection by the earlier right holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GI registration can block later trademarks for similar uses, but prior good-faith trademarks are protected; conflicts are resolved considering reputation, duration of use and risk of misleading consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of use: scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Control of use of GIs and TSGs shall cover any type of operation related to controlling the conformity of their use to registered specifications during production, marketing or distribution stages or their use in the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control extends across the supply chain and market to ensure conformity with registered specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control authority approval and change
rubrics_metrics.description: Control shall be carried out by the control authority specified in the application and whose competence has been approved by the Office. Change of the control authority stated in the register may be made upon approval of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants specify a control body which must be Office‑approved; any later change requires Office approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control reporting frequency and complaint-triggered reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Control reports shall be submitted to the Office once a year after registration is published in the Bulletin. However, in case of complaints, the Office may request earlier submission of the reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reporting is standard; complaints can accelerate oversight and require earlier reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for control deficiencies and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a deficiency is found upon examination of control reports, the registrant shall be notified and asked to correct the deficiencies within six months. If the deficiency is not remedied within the prescribed period or it is determined that control activities were not carried out in line with the procedure, the provisions of Article 43 shall be applied (which can lead to change or cancellation of registrant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Six-month cure period applies to control deficiencies; failure can lead to loss of rights or registrant change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant may recover control costs from controlled parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant may claim the costs related to the controls from the parties subject to those controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control-related expenses can be allocated to producers/parties under the control scheme per the registrant's entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with other control laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The control stated in this Book covers controls made by the control authority established by the applicant and shall not prejudice the provisions of the Law on Veterinary Services Plant Health Food and Feed and other laws related to the control of GIs and TSGs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory GI/TSG control coexists with sectoral public health and veterinary legislation; compliance with all applicable laws is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity: who may request and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity of a GI or TSG may be requested from the court by persons who have interest. The court shall decide invalid if: (a) the register is not in compliance with any one of the conditions set out in Articles 33,34,35,37 or 39; (b) the registration has not been made by those who have right to apply under Article 36; (c) controls are not carried out as set out in Article 49.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidity is a court remedy available to interested parties where substantive eligibility, applicant standing, or control obligations are deficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of invalidity (retroactivity limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a GI/TSG is decided invalid by the court, legal protection provided by this Code is deemed not to have arisen. However, retroactive effects of invalidity shall not extend to: (a) any final judgments for infringement enforced prior to decision of invalidity; (b) contracts concluded and executed prior to the decision of invalidity. Partial or total reimbursement of sums paid under contracts may be claimed on grounds of equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidity annuls statutory protection prospectively with limited retroactivity protections for prior court judgments and executed contracts; equity remedies for contractual payments may remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and cancellation after invalidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Final court decision of invalidity shall be notified to the Office ex officio; the GI/TSG deemed invalid shall be cancelled from the register and information regarding cancellation published in the Bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court decision triggers administrative cancellation and public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of registered rights by registrant
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant may withdraw from the rights provided by the registration and the responsibilities related to inspections. The demand of withdrawal is published in the Bulletin. If a request for change of registrant by eligible parties is not filed within three months after publication, the GI/TSG shall be cancelled from the register. Withdrawal takes effect from date of its entry to the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant-initiated withdrawal triggers publication and a three-month window for replacement claims; absence of replacement leads to cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement acts (explicit list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following uses of a registered geographical sign shall be considered as infringement: (a) any direct or indirect commercial use of a registered GI or emblem in relation to products within the register or comparable products to exploit reputation where they do not carry the properties specified; (b) any deceptive use, replicas or associative use about place of origin or translation of the GI even if accompanied by expressions such as 'style', 'type', 'method', 'as produced in'; (c) any use of false or misleading indication or description about the origin or properties specified in GI register on packaging, promotional material or any written material related to the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This article operationalizes enforcement: reputation exploitation, imitation, misleading origin/quality claims are actionable infringements.
